Enzo Fernandez - What's the latest?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' James Savundra on whether Enzo Fernandez could still leave Stamford Bridge, despite Manchester City missing Chelsea's Friday 'deadline' last week

James Savundra: When I spoke to Xabi Alonso in his second week at work, he was glowing in his praise when it came to players like Reece James and Cole Palmer. But he gave very little away when it came to Enzo Fernandez. He only gave short sentences. The only thing he confirmed was that he was looking forward to working with him, and that he's a great player, but he didn't say much more than that, which made you think that, at that point, the saga [over Fernandez's future] hadn't been resolved.

I know that Fernandez has got a contract for another six years, but I think he wants to be better remunerated for what he offers to the side. As we know with the Chelsea contracts, some of them are very long, but they're more incentivised in terms of performance or if Chelsea go on and win things. I think he wants a higher base salary. That's our understanding.

But when the deadline eventually passed on Friday with no £120m bid from Man City, Chelsea sources said they expected Fernandez to stay until the end of the season. But that's no clear guarantee. They don't want the start of the season, the start of this new era dominated by conversations and questions for Xabi Alonso to answer every press conference. But one thing I will say, if Enzo Fernandez does stay he will be a massive part of Alonso's plans.

Who else could be on the way out before the deadline?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' James Savundra with the latest on Chelsea's potential outgoings this summer transfer window

Will Chelsea play a back three?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' David Richardson discusses how Chelsea could line-up under new boss Xabi Alonso

David Richardson: The big question around Xabi Alonso at Chelsea is whether he would replicate the 3-4-3 formation that he had such great success with at Bayer Leverkusen. Chelsea have played six pre-season games. In their first three, they played a back four, which was similar to what Alonso did at Real Madrid - and, as we know, it didn't go too well there. But since then, in the final three matches, he's played a back three and that has been when more of his senior players have been available to him.

In the first half against Real Sociedad, Chelsea sat too deep in the back three. It became almost a back five, with Marco Palestra and Pedro Neto as their wingbacks. They couldn't get out. They couldn't press. They became sloppy on the ball - and that was despite Morgan Rogers scoring after 10 minutes. They were much improved in the second half. They played higher up the pitch, dominated possession and because they were higher up the pitch, they were able to press.

Can Rogers and Palmer play together?

David Richardson: Rogers was on the left of the front three against Real Sociedad, with Joao Pedro through the middle and Palmer off the right. Rogers and Palmer didn't play as wingers; they were tucked in as inside forwards, which suits their game.

That is some front three. If you compare that to any other team in the league, it's got to be right up there - possibly the best front three in the division. Particularly with the way Joao Pedro is playing - he's scored seven goals in five games in pre-season. Rogers linked up well with Joao Pedro on Saturday, and it was probably him and Joao Pedro that showed more signs of connecting than Rogers and Palmer.

It's all about getting those front three firing. Palmer had that incredible first season at Chelsea and hasn't quite lived up to those standards. But having not been at the World Cup, he's had some rest, a full pre-season now and hopefully he'll be over those injuries that he's had in recent seasons and should be firing. It's a big, big season for him.

Who's the No 1?

David Richardson: It's a reflection on how well Robert Sanchez has started to do that he is still No 1. He had a much improved season last year. He played 51 times, a full season in goal and he looked more confident, more comfortable.

There were big question marks over his playing out from the back - I remember him being heckled by some Chelsea supporters to get the ball forward and just get it away from his own goal. But he's settled down now. Against Real Sociedad on Saturday, he made several saves in the first half, and he seems to be growing into that role.

As for Mike Penders, he came on as a substitute in that game but I think he'll have to wait for his opportunity. For now, it looks like Sanchez is Chelsea's No 1.

Why did Chelsea sign Henderson and Welbeck?

Image: Jordan Henderson signed a two-year deal with Chelsea

James Savundra: There have been so many silly yellow cards and that really did hamper Chelsea and a number of different managers couldn't solve it. Under Alonso and this new leadership group he's forming, when you consider the age of the players brought in, there's clearly been a lot of learning from the ownership group over the last four years.

Sometimes the approach was a bit scattergun when it came to transfers. But now I think Alonso has looked at the squad and realised 'we definitely need more experienced players that know how to win things'. That's players like Henderson and Welbeck, who can help these young players become players who can perform consistently in the Premier League and accept all that comes with being a Chelsea player.

These young players will need to deliver success - but now they've got real role models in the form of those more mature players. And actually even in the signings of Maxence Lacroix, who's 26, and Pep Chavarria, 28, I think it's clear that there's an admission that there have been mistakes made and everybody is seeing this as a new chapter.

What's success for Alonso and Chelsea this season?

James Savundra: It would be fascinating to be in those conversations and whether or not they've laid out clear defined targets for this season. I think they are really seeing this as a long-term project over two, three or four years and as long as they are seeing that progress on the pitch, whether or not they get Champions League football this season, I don't think that will define whether or not Xabi Alonso gets a second year.

It will be whether you can actually see with your eyes that this team is getting there, this culture is being built behind the scenes, because Alonso is going to be involved in a number of different areas at the club. But signing a player like Morgan Rogers for £117m? You're not spending this sort of money in the transfer window to finish in the top 10 or just to get Europa League football.

This season things have really opened up with a number of managerial changes. Liverpool a lot of upheaval there and that squad doesn't quite look ready for the start of the Premier League season. Manchester United, it's their first full season under Michael Carrick and how are they going to cope with playing in the Champions League as well?

So getting into the Champions League and having a really strong cup run in the FA Cup or the Carabao Cup will probably be the aim.

Sports.title: Fifa chief sacked after criticism of Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan
Sports.content:
The Fifa chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, has been sacked after openly criticising Gianni Infantino’s ill-fated plan to sell parts of the World Cup to private investors.

In a significant development at the pinnacle of world football’s deeply troubled governing body, Lamour has departed less than two years after joining from a previous role at Uefa. He had come out strongly against Infantino’s FFE scheme after it was revealed, saying Fifa’s administration had been “deceived” and that the president “believes he embodies Fifa when he is supposed to be at its service”.

Lamour had also made clear that he would countenance losing his job as a consequence of opposing the plan, which was shelved hours after he spoke out on 31 July. “If that means I lose my job, then so be it,” he said in a statement. “I will understand and respect that decision. At least I’ll sleep well tonight.”

The precise circumstances of his sacking are unclear but the Fifa secretary general, Mattias Grafström, informed staff in an email that Lamour would be leaving the organisation.

A Fifa spokesperson said: “Fifa can confirm that the working relationship between Fifa and Kevin Lamour as Fifa’s chief operating officer has ended on 17 August 2026. Fifa thanks Kevin for his two years of service and wishes him the best of luck for the future. No further comment will be made on the matter.”

In the statement that appears to have expedited his departure, Lamour also said his colleagues “deserve better than contempt and intimidation”. He added: “My feeling is that we all want to be proud to work for Fifa, and today, unfortunately, it seems that is no longer the case for many of us.” On the same day one of Infantino’s senior advisers, Carlos Cordeiro, resigned in protest at Infantino’s proposals.

Lamour had been Uefa’s deputy secretary general before joining Fifa, and had first joined the European body in 2007. His departure is all the more eye-catching for his longstanding working relationship with Infantino, with whom he also worked at Uefa. Infantino continues to be under huge pressure after the failure of his scheme, with efforts to force his removal continuing.

Sports.title: Todd Boehly and Mark Walter consider selling Chelsea shares to Clearlake Capital
Sports.content:
The Chelsea chair, Todd Boehly, and director Mark Walter are considering selling their shares in the club to the majority owners, Clearlake Capital, in a deal that would give the private equity company complete control at Stamford Bridge.

Clearlake, whose investment is managed by Behdad Eghbali and José E Feliciano, already owns more than 60% of Chelsea, but in an unusual arrangement agreed when buying the club from Roman Abramovich four years ago, they share operational control with a consortium led by Boehly, who along with Walter and Hansjörg Wyss each own about 13%.

The two ownership groups have been locked in a stalemate for almost two years when reports first emerged that they were seeking to buy each other out following a disagreement over strategy, particularly regarding their plans for a new stadium.

Discussions over a potential deal, which would value the club at more than £5bn, have resumed over the past few weeks however, as first reported by the Financial Times, as Walter is seeking to raise funds to pay off insurers following a US federal investigation over alleged tax fraud.

Walter is being investigated by the US Department of Justice over $21bn in loans which it has been alleged were not disclosed to state insurance regulators, which has led to the sudden sale of assets to pay down some of the loans. Walter last week sold the Los Angeles Lakers to Josh ⁠Kushner and Bob Iger ⁠for $12.5bn just a year after buying the NBA franchise for $10bn, leading to speculation that the 66-year-old may also seek to exit Chelsea.

Boehly and Walter are close friends as well as longstanding business partners, having previously invested together in the LA Dodgers Major League Baseball team and the LA Sparks WNBA franchise.

Together with Wyss, the pair control 38% of Chelsea through Blueco 22 Holdings, although it is unclear whether the Swiss billionaire is also willing to sell. Under the terms of their £2.5bn purchase from Abramovich after the Russian was sanctioned by the UK government following the invasion of Ukraine however, none of Chelsea’s shareholders can sell to a third party without the consent of their partners.

An external sale is therefore unlikely, putting Clearlake in a strong position to gain the complete control it has been seeking for some time, although Boehly and Walter will demand a significant premium on the £325m they paid for their shares four years ago.

View image in fullscreen Todd Boehly leaving would give Behdad Eghbali’s Clearlake Capital effective control of Chelsea. Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

A sale by Boehly and Walter would leave Clearlake with more than 86% of Chelsea’s shares and effective control of the club, including the bid to build a new stadium, which they want to locate at Stamford Bridge.

Walter has been a silent and barely visible partner at Chelsea, but Boehly was the public face of the club following the 2022 takeover and acted as interim sporting director during that year’s summer transfer window, leading the purchase of players such as Raheem Sterling and Marc Cucurella.

Boehly stepped back from that hands-on role after 12 months, with Eghbali taking more operational control on behalf of Clearlake, but has often been blamed by Chelsea fans for the side’s underperformance.

Boehly was due to stand down as chair at the end of the season, with a Clearlake representative to replace him for the next five years under the terms of the ownership agreement.

The timing of an exit at this stage would be ironic, as after spending years investing heavily in young players with resale value at Clearlake’s behest, Chelsea have returned to Boehly’s original strategy this summer by signing experienced players such as Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson.

Representatives of Clearlake, Boehly and Chelsea were approached for comment.

Sports.title: Rodri calls it ‘a dream to play for Barcelona’ as he flies in for medical
Sports.content:
Rodri has said it is “a dream” to play for Barcelona after landing in Catalonia on Monday to complete his move from Manchester City. Spain’s World Cup-winning captain will have a medical on Tuesday after City accepted Barcelona’s third bid of £65.4m.

“Very happy to arrive,” Rodri said at Barcelona’s El Prat airport. “There have been some very intense days, but I’m happy that everything has been resolved. For me it’s a dream to play for Barcelona. I’m excited about being with my teammates, many of them I already know. Now it’s time to get to work and give my best.”

The 30-year-old had entered the final year of his contract at the Etihad Stadium and made it clear he would like the opportunity to move to Barcelona. City, who are now closing in on a deal to sign Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, were reluctant sellers but had little choice with Rodri out of contract next summer.

City had already rejected Barcelona’s bid of around €60m (£51m) for Rodri last week after an initial offer of €45m (£38.5m) but have now accepted the latest bid.

Speaking after City’s 3-0 Community Shield defeat by Arsenal on Sunday, Enzo Maresca called Rodri a “top player” and said “all the teams need Rodri”, but City have been unable to persuade their linchpin to stay and sign a new contract. Rodri had only returned to the club on Friday, having undergone back surgery after the World Cup, with Maresca saying he had given him a “big hug” when he first met up with him.

Rodri has spent seven seasons with City, winning the Premier League four times and scoring the only goal when they beat Inter in the 2023 Champions League final. The following year he won the Ballon d’Or but, by the time he was presented with the trophy, he was sidelined with an anterior cruciate ligament which ruled him out of most of the 2024-25 campaign, while hamstring and groin problems limited him to 33 appearances in Pep Guardiola’s final campaign in charge.

City have already undergone major changes in midfield this summer, spending £116m on Elliot Anderson, while agreeing a deal to sell Tijjani Reijnders to Al Qadsiah. They are now ready to seal a move for the Morocco star Bouaddi.

The teenager impressed at the World Cup and Lille had initially wanted any potential move to include a 12-month loan deal back to the French side. However, with City losing Bernardo Silva and now Rodri, Maresca is keen to bulk up his midfield options for the new campaign and want Bouaddi available for this season. City have also been linked with Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández and retain an interest.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca’s Manchester City opener was startlingly bad
Sports.content:
There are caveats. It was only the Community Shield – and no side has gone on to win the league after lifting the Community Shield since 2018. It was against the league champions, whose pre-season has involved far less strenuous travel than their own. By the time the season really gets going, there will be greater clarity in central midfield, with Rodri set to complete his move to Barcelona imminently. But this was a startlingly bad opening for Enzo Maresca at Manchester City.

Succeeding a manager of Pep Guardiola’s stature is never easy, as numerous clubs have found. But it’s not just Guardiola’s stature, the sense that whoever follows him stands in his shadow. It’s that his style of play is so idiosyncratic that the transition process inevitably becomes more difficult. Even though Maresca was Guardiola’s assistant at City in 2022-23, and his football is Guardiola-inspired, it is not identical, not least because Guardiola was always evolving. Even allowing for all that, though, it was remarkable how poorly City defended in their 3-0 defeat by Arsenal on Sunday.

Arsenal played well. There was a sharpness to them and a slickness to their passing that wasn’t always present last season. Fears that they may have lost their appetite having ended their 22-year wait for the title may have been overstated (although much, much tougher tests await). But City were a rabble, limited going forward and a shambles at the back.

It was the second goal that will really have worried them, because Arsenal had to do so little to score. Martin Ødegaard was given time to measure his cross. Christos Tzolis wandered off the back of Abdukodir Khusanov. Then Kai Havertz, slightly more explicably, pulled away from Rúben Dias. In Khusanov’s defence, it probably should be acknowledged that he does not usually play at right-back, but he has occupied the role before. A wide player drifting off your back should not come as a shock; perhaps it’s just pre-season and he was not as alert as he will be, but it was a baffling error. But it was of a piece with the wider whole; throughout, City seemed off the pace, not as focused as Arsenal. Even if that improves as the season goes on, it’s a problem if City have title aspirations; how far clear will Arsenal be by the time City finally click – if they do click?

But there were structural issues on that flank as well. Antoine Semenyo was barely involved. Elliot Anderson, on the right of the midfield two, was unable to check the forward surges of Riccardo Calafiori, who scored the first and whose run played a key role in the third. An attacking left-back, even one with as much freedom to drift infield as the Italian enjoys, shouldn’t cause that much trouble.

The midfield issue desperately needs resolving. Rodri was an unused substitute as talks about his possible likely move to Barcelona go on (City accepted a bid for him on Sunday night). It’s not just his quality that will be missed; his organisational abilities will be too. Enzo Fernández, who worked with Maresca at Chelsea, did seem to have been lined up as a replacement for Rodri but City did not submit a bid before the Friday 5pm deadline Chelsea had placed for selling the midfielder. Mateo Kovacic spent much of last season deputising for Rodri but he is 32 now; he is not the future. Factor in the loss of Bernardo Silva as well, and there is a serious shortfall in midfield.

Generally, in fact, City’s squad looks a little short. Dias and Marc Guéhi are the only defenders over 25. There are plenty of attacking midfielders but Omar Marmoush has never really convinced as a back-up to Erling Haaland. The £200m spree in January 2025 may have helped stop the rot, but the players who came in then – not just Marmoush and Khusanov but also Vitor Reis and Nico González – would not be badly missed now. City, once so focused in their spending, have started to make mistakes. Tijjani Reijnders, brought in last summer for £50m, is about to be shipped on. Rayan Aït-Nouri was a baffling signing when he arrived and nothing in the past year has changed that view.

Maresca must have looked at Arsenal’s squad, the extraordinary options available to Mikel Arteta in midfield, and despaired. Put generously, his is a squad in transition, although it’s starting to look as though it may be a squad in decline. The sense over the past couple of years was of Guardiola, slowly, passing his peak, but in retrospect perhaps it was only his genius that kept an ailing City competitive.

The evidence of Sunday, with all due caveats about the stage of the season, is that this may be a very bad time for Maresca to have replaced Guardiola. Taking over from a legend would be extremely challenging in the best of circumstances, and these are starting to look like they may be very bad circumstances.

Sports.title: Premier League to allow audio of conversations between players and referees
Sports.content:
The Premier League will permit audio of on-field conversations between players and referees during live broadcasts for the first time this season.

The use of audio by the Premier League’s domestic TV rights holders, Sky Sports and TNT Sports, is part of an expansion of the RefCam system, which became a permanent feature of top-flight coverage last season after a six-week trial at the start of the campaign. The head-mounted RefCams were used by broadcasters to ­provide near‑instant replays of match ­incidents from a new angle in an attempt to enhance the viewer experience, but under the terms of their agreement with clubs the audio captured by the cameras was not televised until several days later.

The regulations will be relaxed this season, however, to permit a limited use of RefCam audio during live matches, with one or two incidents to be broadcast from each of the Premier League’s 38 match rounds.

The audio will not be broadcast live or include any incidents that are referred to the video assistant referee, as that is not permitted under the laws of the game, which are set by the International Football Association Board (Ifab). The new audio offering will be made available as part of near-live instant replays, however, while the number of TV games featuring RefCam will increase from 20 to about 45. The audio experiment will be trialled first before being rolled out and will not feature on the Premier League’s opening weekend.

Football has been slow to replicate the broadcasting innovations embraced by other sports, with in-match interviews and dressing room cameras long since accepted in cricket and both codes of rugby, as well as many American sports. Under increasing pressure from rights holders, football is belatedly looking to open up.

Sports.title: Sergio’s stunner lights up El Sardinero on Racing Santander’s emotional La Liga return | Sid Lowe
Sports.content:
“The poor kid couldn’t believe what had happened; none of us could have if we’d just done what he had just done,” said Álvaro Mantilla, Racing Santander’s captain in the match they had longed for more than anything in the world. Which was why the kid – a 19-year-old from just along the coast who had been at the club half his life – wasn’t the only one crying. The day Sergio Martínez played his first game for Racing, he had climbed into the stand to hug his grandad; the day he played his first in primera, on Sunday afternoon at the Sardinero, he just about managed to stand before it, legs giving way a little and tears coming to his eyes. All around him they felt it too, 22,413 people absolutely losing it.

What he had just done was, well, everything. At least that’s how it felt right then. “Euphoria”, his captain called it. In his first game in the first division, his third start ever, Sergio hadn’t just scored; he had scored the kind of goal you get in a comic, all explosions and exclamation marks. The ball sat up like an invitation and Kapow! – Sergio smashed it on the bounce, a cartoon arrow drawn to the top corner. It tore through the air and through time, flashing past at 126km an hour and 14 years a second, so Sergio ran to the corner, holding the badge he has worn since he was 10. There, there was a wobble as it came to him just what he had done. Bloody hell, this was actually happening.

The teenager won’t even remember the last time Racing were in the first division: he was five. This was not just Sergio’s first top-flight game, it was Mantilla’s too – he was born and raised 5km away. And it was Jorge Salinas’ first as well, another 19-year-old from Santander. Sergio Canales, an academy kid from Santander like them, had played there and with Racing but that was 16 years ago, when he was a teenager too, the most eligible in Spain. Thirty-five now, he had at last come home. In almost the entire time he had been away, so had his club. Sunday afternoon was the first time that Racing, founder members of the first division, had played a top-flight game since 2012. And here they were 2-0 up against Villarreal, the redemption real.

It didn’t last long but it will last for a very, very long time. Leading 1-0 through a penalty from Andrés Martín, Sergio made it 2-0 in the 34th minute. They had deserved it too: “The energy was unstoppable,” Villarreal coach Iñigo Pérez admitted. For 44 minutes, Racing were something like perfection. And then in 67 seconds, two flashes from Pape Gueye and Nicholas Pépé had taken it away again – a reminder, Racing’s coach José Alberto López said, of what the first division is, how unforgiving it can be. Except this wasn’t going to be taken away: not the point, a 2-2 draw against the team that finished third last season which could be decisive in what will surely still be a fight for survival, and not the moment, their day.

View image in fullscreen Teenager Sergio Martínez extended Racing Santander’s lead before being pegged back by Villarreal. Photograph: Cesar Ortiz Gonzalez/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

El Sardinero, more ground than stadium, built in the late 1980s and with something about it that’s happily still there with corner floodlights touching the sky, was packed again. Along the waterfront they had come, the only people not in white Racing shirts those in green ones: a city, a community built, heading back to where they belong. If they were home, so was the first division: this was one of those days that everyone else could celebrate too. “I loved it,” said Pérez, and he coaches their opponents. “I’m so happy to come here and see all the emotion and the excitement. This is a joy for anyone who comes.” But more than a historic club being in the first division for the first time since 2012, this was about being, full stop.

Relegated in 2012 after a decade in the top flight, having played in Europe just three and a half years earlier and beaten Manchester City along the way, Racing fell a long way, and might never have got up again.

At all.

They were relegated again immediately and spent seven of the next 10 years in Segunda B, Spain’s theoretically amateur third-to-seventh-tier with its 80 teams and four groups. Worse, their fight for survival was not just about sport. By then, the financial and institutional crisis was out of control. The debt had reached over €40m. €14m was owed to the state and players and staff went unpaid. In July 2011 they filed for bankruptcy, opening up an administration process. In an era when the club’s shirt sponsor was for a brand of chorizo, slang for thief, two presidents would eventually get jail sentences for embezzlement of club funds – and that doesn’t include Ahsan Ali Syed.

Francisco Pernía and Ángel Lavín were the men charged. Between them came “Mr Ali”, welcomed as a saviour in the winter of 2011, championed by Pernía and the leader of the Cantabrian government, Miguel Ángel Revilla, who declared: “The Hindu has his pockets full of cash.” Ali spent €3.5m on the buyout and said there was space alongside Real Madrid and Barcelona for Racing. Instead they ended up in a league with Langreo, Durango and Calahorra. He, meanwhile, had disappeared entirely, wanted by Interpol and finally arrested almost a decade later for fraud.

View image in fullscreen Jorge Salinas, 19, was another young Racing Santander making his La Liga debut. Photograph: Cesar Ortiz Gonzalez/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

With Lavín taking over, Racing’s crisis deepened, the sense that the end was coming. In January 2014, fans stormed the directors’ box and tried to force Lavín out. Then, a fortnight later, their players walked on to the pitch for the quarter-finals of the Copa del Rey against Real Sociedad. Still in Segunda B, they had beaten two first division sides but instead of playing they just stood there with their arms around each other’s shoulders. There was a dignity in their defiance, a solidarity.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

With Lavín at last forced out, former player Manolo Higuera stepping in in 2015, there was the start of a revival: a decency, an honesty, a seriousness about confronting their reality. Something was forged by being on the edge too, but they hadn’t stepped back from it entirely. When club legend Pedro Munitis became coach in 2015, it wasn’t just that he wasn’t paid, it was that he, like others at the club, was paying: players’ wages, and even travel costs were coming out of his pocket. More than 50 legal cases still hung over them. The club was “dead and buried”, Higuera admits, little they could do; that they came through it was “a miracle”. They only played one of the next three seasons in the second division and although they went up in 2022, when José Alberto López took over as coach that December, there was a risk that they would slip back down again. Instead, he secured survival. Then seventh, then a playoff place, and then the title.

José Alberto said that to begin with Racing were still closer to being an amateur side, “more neighbourhood team than professional club”. He admitted that he wondered what he had got himself into, but he helped them get out of it. Having been forced to give up playing at 20 because of rheumatism, José Alberto had begun at the bottom, working at Ikea while he coached in Asturias; now his approach carried Racing. Brave and attacking, his team would go for opponents; this was going to be fun too, that was non-negotiable. Even last year when they won the second division, they conceded 61 goals. A momentum built that would eventually bring them up. Optimism was back at last, on and off the pitch.

Quick Guide La Liga results and fixtures Show Alavés 3-0 Getafe, Espanyol 3-0 Levante, Racing Santander 2-2 Villarreal, Sevilla 2-1 Rayo Vallecano Monday Deportivo La Coruña v Elche (8pm BST) Wednesday Atlético Madrid v Malaga (8pm BST) Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

That summer Higuera convinced Sebastián Ceria to get involved. The time was right: Ceria, a social democrat Argentinian philanthropist with a PhD in mathematics from Carnegie and a professor at Columbia, had just sold his company for $850m. His wife, Alicia Zorrilla, is from Cantabria and friends with Higuera’s wife. Ceria bought a controlling stake for €30m, bringing a new mentality built around the people – and above all stability. In December 2024, the final administration payments were met, their debts paid off 13 years on. Assets that had been stripped have been recovered, so too has the pride, a sense of belonging. With Ceria describing football as “democratising”, the shift is visible in the shirts all across the city.

It had started with a lunch in London. This Sunday Higuera and Ceria sat in the stand at the Sardinero together and watched Racing Santander play in the first division once again. And they watched the side play the way the coach that transformed them always said they would: no backing down, no doubt that primera is their place too. They saw the flags along the roof – every first division team there, them too – and heard the fans belt out La Fuente de Cacho at the start of the day they had waited a lifetime for. They saw fans lead the way alongside the Cantabrian sea and Mantilla lead the way out of the tunnel, armband on. They saw Sergio announce his arrival and all of theirs, not alone in feeling the tears. And Canales, who had announced his departure at the same age, standing before supporters singing songs of redemption and return. “It was … strange,” Canales said, somehow speaking for all of them too. “I can’t quite assimilate this still. I could feel the hairs standing on end. Above all, what I feel is gratitude.”

Sports.title: ‘I’ll remember it for the rest of my life’: the footballers whose biggest games come before their league begins
Sports.content:
Premier League footballers are gearing up for the start of the season, but some of their fellow professionals in smaller leagues across Europe have been going all summer – even those who play a winter campaign. Some played the biggest games of their lives when the rest of us were watching the World Cup. The Champions League qualifiers began when the World Cup was at the last-16 stage, with some clubs already knocked out of Europe by the time England were beaten by Argentina in Atlanta.

Larne, the champions of Northern Ireland, began their European crusade on the day Argentina beat Egypt in the World Cup last-16, Dan Bent’s penalty in the second leg a week later helping them overcome Tre Fiori of San Marino in the Champions League. Larne’s reward was a meeting with former European champions Red Star Belgrade. They were beaten 9-0 on aggregate by the Serbian giants, but it is an experience Bent will treasure for ever.

“Red Star was probably the biggest game in the club’s history,” says the centre-back. “When the draw came out, we were ecstatic. You want to play those games in those stadiums. Everyone tells you about how long the tunnel is and how intimidating it is, and then you’re there and a part of it. There were 27,000 fans and the funny thing is, for them, that’s a medium-sized crowd. The stadium was only half-full.” The population of Larne could have fit into the rest of it with room to spare.

View image in fullscreen Dan Bent playing for Larne at Red Star Belgrade in the Champions League qualifiers. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

“Red Star were just another level,” he says. “You don’t realise until you’re in amongst it. You do your best, but sometimes there are gaps that are hard to bridge. But to play in that competition, at that ground, against a team as big as that, was amazing. I’ll remember it for the rest of my life.”

The European qualifiers move fast, with teams given little time to prepare or analyse opponents. “It’s a privilege to play in Champions League qualifiers but a lot of uncertainty comes with that,” says Bent. “In early June you know your first Champions League game would be around the first week of July, so you can gear up for that. But after that, each week will just change depending on results.

“One minute, we could be heading to Rangers or Slovakia, the next we’re going to Gibraltar or Cyprus. You might be playing one team who could play in a totally different way to the other, or we might want to play in a different way against them. You need to pick up things quickly. It’s a quick turnaround. Logistically, it is pretty crazy. You have to plan for all eventualities.”

If players find it unnerving, imagine the stress for the clubs’ operations managers and the players’ families. “I’ve got a partner and two children and it is hard for them,” says Bent. “She’s very supportive and understands, but it doesn’t get any easier knowing I’m away for three days, then the week after I could be flying out again to another country. It helps when you have a good family around you who understand the demands of football. They know it’s a positive thing because not many people are able to play in Champions League qualifiers.”

Bent is used to living out of a suitcase and jumping on a plane every few days. He grew up in Kent and started his career at Gillingham. After being released in 2015 when he was a teenager, he took a scholarship in America. He played college and semi-professional soccer in Georgia, Ohio and South Carolina before moving to Gibraltar to play for Magpies, Manchester 62 and then Lincoln Red Imps – who are Larne’s next European opponents.

After losing to Red Star in the Champions League, Larne dropped into the Europa League qualifiers where they were narrowly beaten in extra time by Georgian club Iberia 1999. Now they face the Gibraltan champions over two legs for a place in the Conference League group stage, the first leg on Thursday seeing an emotional return for Bent, who spent long enough in Gibraltar to become eligible for the national team and earn 17 caps.

View image in fullscreen Dan Bent celebrates after converting a penalty against Tre Fiori in the Champions League first qualifying round in July. Photograph: Inpho/Shutterstock

The tie is a huge opportunity for both clubs. Larne beat the Red Imps at this stage two years ago and booked their place in the Conference League group stage, securing €2.6m in prize money. Considering that clubs are awarded around £50,000 for winning the league in Northern Ireland and just £20,000 for winning the cup, that is transformational money for the club and players – who earn hefty bonuses for European victories.

“There’s a big core of boys who were here when they got to the group phase, so they talk about that,” says Bent. “They played games all the way up until Christmas. They’ve been there and they want to go back.” The group stage is also a prominent shop window. It’s not just Bodø/Glimt players who are earning transfers off the back of repeated impressive performances in European competitions.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Being able to drop through Uefa’s three tiers can be a gamechanger for players’ careers. “That’s where the hard work of winning the league previously comes to fruition,” says Bent. “You go through the whole year to win the league, to make sure you’ll have a summer of European football. If you go out of the Champions League, you’re going to be dropping down and having a few games. I do enjoy that.”

These second and third chances mean a lot of players are racking up considerable European records. “I’m probably up there in terms of European experience,” says Bent, who will play in Europe for the 21st time when Larne visit Gibraltar on Thursday night. “Our goalkeeper, Rohan Ferguson, has something like 40 appearances in Europe. We have boys who’ve been great servants in the league but haven’t played a lot of European football, and young lads with that fresh hunger, wanting to play in it. It’s a well-balanced group.”

Larne kicked off their title defence with a hard-fought goalless draw at Coleraine over the weekend and the second leg of their tie against Lincoln Red Imps next week will be their 10th match in five competitions this season. But you won’t hear them complaining. They are having life-enriching experiences on their European expeditions.

This is an article by Gavin Willacy for Playing in the Shadows

Sports.title: Brighton’s Emilie Joramo: ‘I feel like I’m now in the place I want to be’
Sports.content:
Emilie Joramo has long had her sights set on the Women’s Super League, but she held herself back from pushing for a move over from Scandinavia – until now.

“I’d been interested in the league for a long time now and it was a goal for me to get here one day,” says Joramo, who Brighton signed on a free transfer at the end of June. “It was about finding the right path for me to get here. I didn’t want to go too early, I wanted to feel ready for it both physically and mentally. Now, everything just felt right.”

Brighton had been tracking the Norwegian midfielder for some time and the 24-year-old was aware of their interest. An encouraging conversation with Brighton’s manager, Dario Vidosic, and good meetings with the club as her contract with Hammarby drew closer to its end meant she was at last ready to join the league she had followed from afar.

That time in Sweden with Hammarby, with whom she reached the Europa Cup final last season, and before that in her homeland with Rosenborg who she helped win the Norwegian Cup for the first time in 21 years, was crucial in preparing her for her latest challenge.

“I had so much fun at Hammarby and I’ve got so many good friends there,” she says. “I grew both as a football player and as a person in those years. I didn’t feel ready when I was 21, when I went to Sweden, to come over here. I felt like I needed to play a bit more, to play every game, that was really important for me.”

That Brighton had been aware of her for some time was a boost too. “It’s reassuring for me that they really wanted me,” she says. “They hadn’t just watched a couple games, they’d been following me for years, and that’s really important to me because I’m not going to jump at the first opportunity I get. I like to think things through and it has to feel right for me.”

View image in fullscreen Emilie Joramo played Champions League qualifying last year, and helped Hammarby reach the final of the inaugural Europa Cup Photograph: Emma Wallskog/Bildbyrån/Shutterstock

For Brighton fans wondering what they are getting, there should be some excitement too. Joramo is fiercely motivated and feels she fits the possession-based style of football that Vidosic wants his team to play.

“I would say that I’m a hardworking player,” she says, when asked to describe herself. “I always give 100% all of the time. I can’t do 50, 60, 70, I’m always 100%. I want to have the ball. I want to play, not just put balls in behind but to keep the ball , play with each other, [build] good relationships with the other players and think several steps ahead. They’ve always been things that I’m good at and I’m always wanting to get better at too.”

Brighton and the WSL present a step up. “I think I can get challenged a lot here because things go much faster, the intensity is higher, you have a smaller amount of time when you have the ball,” she says. “So, it’s a perfect place for me to be at now to be challenged further and develop my strengths but also the parts that I’m not as strong at and need to develop more.”

Arriving and starting life on the south coast was “a bit overwhelming” in the beginning: “There’s so many people to get to know, the staff is so much bigger than what I’ve been used to. So, instead of one physio you have five and you need to get to know everyone and get to know which person does which role. That’s always the way it is in a new team, of course, but it’s much bigger here.”

Everyone has been very welcoming and her first impressions of training sessions under Vidosic have been positive. “I’ve only had two sessions with him so far,” she says, “but he seems very, very good at football tactics, how the game works, how to play good football, and that was important for me because I’m a player that wants to have the ball and always wants to try to get better and try to play good football together as a team, not only as individuals. This is what Dario wants, so it really fits my ambitions, my values and how I want to play.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Emilie Joramo was Brighton’s second signing of the summer window – they have since added five more. Photograph: James Boardman/Brighton and Hove Albion

She is finding her feet on the pitch, and starting to find them off it. Joramo’s girlfriend has moved to England with her, which has helped the transition and helps her escape football when needed. “I have to have other things to do besides football,” she says. “We’ve been to the beach and have been exploring the city. It’s so different for me to live by the beach, I’m from the mountains and the woods. This is like a holiday for me, and with the weather as well, it’s been so warm. It’s really nice.”

The goal now is “to contribute as much as I can to this team and play as much as I can”, but Joramo’s patience as she worked towards her WSL goal should continue to serve her well. “I feel like I’m now in the place I want to be and develop in and I need to give it a bit of time in the beginning, because I can be very impatient,” she says. “I have to give it some time to get into it, get into the intensity and everything around the game here, because it’s so much more than what I’m used to in Sweden, this is so much bigger.”

At the end of her first season in England is a big carrot, should Norway come through a two-legged playoff against Romania and then another against Albania or Wales and qualify for the 2027 Women’s World Cup.

Joramo made her debut for the senior side in 2022 and has been on the fringes of the squad since, making three appearances in total and playing for the under-23s. In April she was on the bench for the senior side’s back-to-back qualification campaign wins over Slovenia and she is hopeful her WSL move helps her show what she can bring.

“Hopefully this also will strengthen my opportunities with the national team,” she says. “I know this is the best league in the world, so if I get to play here, then I’ve done something right, I think.”

Sports.title: Man United stand firm on captain Bruno Fernandes' transfer stance as Galatasaray 'prepare stunning DOUBLE-your-money salary offer' and £43m bid for Portugal international
Sports.content:
Man United stand firm on captain Bruno Fernandes' transfer stance as Galatasaray 'prepare stunning DOUBLE-your-money salary offer' and £43m bid for Portugal international

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United insist Bruno Fernandes is not for sale at any price this summer.

Galatasaray, Atletico Madrid, Juventus and AC Milan, are among the clubs who have been weighing up making an offer for the United captain.

Indeed, it is understood Galatasaray are ready to put forward a £42.7million offer for the 31-year-old plus a substantial increase on his salary.

A £57m release clause in the Portugal international's contract for foreign clubs expired last month and United know it would take considerably more to replace him, especially in the current inflated market.

As yet, no offer has been received, and senior United sources say interested parties would be wasting their time. Daily Mail Sport revealed in March that United were planning to instigate talks over a new deal for Fernandes. As it stands, talks remain at the preliminary stage.

Galatasaray and other suitors believe the lack of a new contract for Fernandes is a weak spot they can exploit.

Manchester United are readying themselves for a £42.7million swoop for their captain Bruno Fernandes from Galatasaray

Fernandes has one year left on his current deal with an option for a further year. He is already one of the best paid players in the club, behind Marcus Rashford, on around £220,000 a week.

The club captain was, however, hurt by the club's stance last year when Al Hilal were prepared to offer £100m for him.

The club said it was up to Fernandes whether he wanted to leave and the Portugal international felt they should have expressed a greater desire to keep him, to underline his importance.

Fernandes went on to achieve a Premier League record 21 assists last season and is favourite to be crowned PFA Player of the Year for 2025-26 in Manchester next week.

Despite the allure of greater riches in Saudi Arabia or elsewhere, his ambition has been to stay at Old Trafford and see if he can realise his ambition of leading United to a Premier League title challenge.

Throught the turmoil of Ruben Amorim's tenure and the revival under Michael Carrick, Fernandes has remained close to each coach and been a model professional leading by example on the pitch.

Fernandes, who will be speaking to an audience of fans at invite-only event at Manchester's Arndale centre on Tuesday, said earlier this summer: 'It's not a question of loyalty. I could have gone two years ago, I could have gone three years ago, I could have gone last season, but I really like to be here.

'I think that being successful at this club is something that I can never get at another club. The joy and everything I get, the day I get what I want from this club, I don't think I will get that from any other club in the world.' He told Sky Sports.

Michael Carrick's side, however, insist the 31-year-old is not available for transfer at any price

'I won the Carabao Cup and the FA Cup (but) what this club wants, what these fans want and what I want, myself and the team, we haven't got that yet. Until my contract expires, I'm going to try.'

According to The Telegraph, Dursun Ozbek, the Galatasaray president, is on a mission to sign Fernandes and is prepared to essentially double his money.

The wage on offer is £18.3m annually, which, due to Turkey’s relaxed tax system, means he would take home twice what he earns at United.

The report suggests an offer from Galatasaray would feature an initial bid plus add-ons.

Performance-related add-ons reportedly include £1.3m for every title win up to £5.1m, plus £1.7m if Fernandes is the league’s top assister in his first season or £1.3m if he achieves the accolade in his second.

They could also include £850,000 if Galatasaray qualify for next season’s Champions League, plus another £850,000 if they reach the last-16 and £3m if they reach the quarter-finals.

United are continuing to look for at least one more signing this summer to strengthen Carrick's hand.

They have bid for Leicester City midfielder Louis Page, along with Arsenal, and want a left-back to compete with Luke Shaw.

However, one midfielder who may yet leave is Toby Collyer who has attracted enquiries from West Bromwich Albion. Discussions are at an early stage over a permanent move.

Sports.title: FIFA chief operating officer sacked weeks after accusing president Gianni Infantino of having 'deceived' staff over controversial World Cup sell-off plans
Sports.content:
Kevin Lamour, the FIFA chief operating officer who broke ranks and criticised president Gianni Infantino over his World Cup sell-off plan, has been sacked.

The French-Swiss executive had released an explosive statement declaring that staff had been ‘deceived’ by under-fire Infantino following his now-abandoned proposal, which would have seen stakes in the tournament sold to private investors.

He would now appear to have paid the price.

A FIFA spokesperson said: ‘FIFA can confirm that the working relationship between FIFA and Kevin Lamour as FIFA’s Chief Operating Officer has ended on 17 August 2026.

‘FIFA thanks Kevin for his two years of service and wishes him the best of luck for the future.

‘No further comment will be made on the matter.’

FIFA confirmed chief operating officer Kevin Lamour, centre, has left, weeks after accusing president Gianni Infantino of having 'deceived' staff over plans to sell stakes in the World Cup

Lamour had declared the plans were a 'project of one person' as he criticisted Infantino, pictured, while acknowledging he was willing to lose his job by speaking out

FIFA'S LETTER TO STAFF Dear FIFA Vice Presidents, dear members of the FIFA Council, I hope you are keeping well. I would like to provide you with an important update regarding a change within the FIFA Administration. Following recent discussions, FIFA and our Chief Operating Officer, Kevin Lamour have agreed to part ways. This decision was made after careful consideration and with great respect for Kevin, both personally and professionally. Kevin joined FIFA in November 2024 and in this time has overseen a period of significant change, including improved relationships with stakeholders and the delivery of several significant projects of joint interest, amongst many other key achievements. You will have seen Kevin present in each FIFA Council meeting since his appointment in 2024, and many of you will have had a regular working relationship with Kevin on projects of various kinds since his joining FIFA. I felt it was important that I personally provide you this update and I would like to express my gratitude to Kevin for these contributions and for his work and commitment on behalf of FIFA on a daily basis. I wish Kevin all the best for the future. I look forward to seeing you again shortly and, of course, remain at your full disposal should you have any questions on this or any other matter. All the very best, Mattias Grafström FIFA Secretary General

Staff were made aware of Lamour’s abrupt departure in an email sent by general secretary Mattias Grafstrom on Tuesday night. It has been claimed to Daily Mail Sport that Grafstrom – rather than Infantino – delivered the bullet to Lamour. FIFA have been contacted for comment on the claim.

In the wake of the sell-off plan being made public, Lamour told the Associated Press ‘It is the project of one person. Not only must this project not go ahead … but the time has now come for football political leaders to ask themselves the right questions and make the right decisions.’

Lamour also said that he was prepared to lose his job over speaking out publicly.

‘If that means I lose my job, then so be it,’ his statement to AP added. ‘I will understand and respect that decision. At least I’ll sleep well tonight.’

Lamour follows Infantino’s senior advisor Carlos Cordeiro out of the door. He resigned in July citing his opposition to the controversial plans.

Sports.title: West Ham set to land Joel Piroe on loan, Guglielmo Vicario jets in to Turin as Tottenham agree deal with Juventus... and Rodri closes in on four-year Barcelona contract: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
West Ham set to land Joel Piroe on loan, Guglielmo Vicario jets in to Turin as Tottenham agree deal with Juventus... and Rodri closes in on four-year Barcelona contract: WINDOW WATCH

For all of yesterday's developments - including Al Hilal targeting Chelsea's Pedro Neto - click HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Fullkrug heading for the exit at West Ham

West Ham striker Niclas Fullkrug is ready to take a pay cut to push through his return to former club Werder Bremen.

The striker has been granted permission to travel to Germany ahead of an initial loan move.

The deal includes an option to buy, and Fullkrug is willing to give up part of his salary to help the move happen.

The 33-year-old, who has a contract with West Ham until 2028, is returning to the club where he started his professional career.

He spent last season loan to AC Milan scoring one goal in 20 games.

He cost West Ham £27m from Dortmund in 2024 and scored three goals.

Marseille have made an approach to take West Ham defender Jean-Clair Todibo on loan.

Liverpool yet to receive approach for Bajcetic

Liverpool have yet to receive an offer or enquiry from Getafe for midfielder Stefan Bajcetic.

The 21-year-old has one year left on contact and spent part of last season on loan at Las Palmas.

Madrid-based Getafe have been credited with interest but are yet to make a move.

Awoniyi completes move to newly promoted Coventry

Coventry City have completed the £9million signing of Taiwo Awoniyi from Nottingham Forest.

The Nigeria international was given a send-off at the City Ground during Forest's 2-0 pre-season win over Brest on Sunday.

Awoniyi spent four seasons at Forest, scoring 21 goals in 90 Premier League appearances.

Nottingham Forest paid tribute to Taiwo Awoniyi on Sunday ahead of his move to Coventry

Man United youngster heads for the EFL

Manchester United forward Ethan Ennis is joining Stockport County.

The 21-year-old has agreed a permanent deal for an undisclosed fee with add ons plus a 50percent sell-on and buy-back clause, while United retain matching rights too.

Ennis joined United's academy in 2021 and was in their FA Youth Cup-winning squad the following year, before being promoted to the Under-21s.

He got his first taste of senior football with a loan to Doncaster Rovers, and last season appeared 46 times as part of a temporary switch to Fleetwood Town, scoring six goals and providing eight assists.

He will link up with another former United academy product James Bailey at Edgeley Park, who secured a contract with Jimmy McNulty's side earlier this summer, following the expiry of his deal at United.

Brighton reject Rangers offer for winger

Brighton have rejected a £7.5million offer from Rangers for winger Amario Cozier-Duberry.

The winger spent last season on loan at Bolton.

Man United to rebuff Fernandes interest

Manchester United have no plans to sell Bruno Fernandes before next month's transfer deadline.

Galatasaray, Atletico Madrid, Juventus and AC Milan, are among the clubs who have been weighing up an offer for the United captain.

It is understood Galatasaray are ready to put forward £42.7million for the 31-year-old but his intention has been to stay and see if he can realise his ambition of leading United to a Premier League title challenge.

For more on this story click HERE

Man United will rebuff approaches for Bruno Fernandes amid interest from Galatasaray

It's nearly Hammer time for Piroe

Leeds United have given Joel Piroe permission to travel to West Ham for a medical.

The striker is expected to travel this evening ahead of finalising his move to the Championship club.

With AZ Alkmaar digging in their heels over their valuation of Troy Parrott, the Hammers moved for Piroe on a loan deal, with an obligation to buy.

Joel Piroe is set to say goodbye to Leeds and join West Ham on loan

Ipswich land Ouattara from Strasbourg

Ipswich have confirmed the signing of versatile 20-year-old Abdoul Ouattara, reuniting him with manager Gary O'Neil.

Daily Mail Sport previously reported how the Tractor Boys have been closing in on a deal for Ouattara and team-mate Julio Enciso, 22. The pair worked with O'Neil at Strasbourg last season, before O'Neil left to replace Kieran McKenna at Portman Road.

O'Neil said: 'Abdoul is a talented young player who can play in different positions, so is a very good addition to our squad. We enjoyed working with him in France last season and are delighted to have the opportunity to do so again at Ipswich.'

Canaries making progress on Musaba talks

Norwich City are advancing in talks to sign Fenerbahce winger Anthony Musaba on a season's loan.

The 25-year-old Dutchman, formerly played for Sheffield Wednesday, is due to arrive tonight ahead of a medical.

Norwich want a winger as Ali Ahmed has injured an anterior cruciate ligament.

City work on Bouaddi deal

Manchester City and Lille working to get a deal for £85m-rated Ayyoub Bouaddi over the line.

As Daily Mail Sport reported over the weekend, Lille have been fighting to keep the midfielder for one more season, but City and the player want to seal a move now.

Lille coach Davide Ancelotti explained why Bouaddi is wanted by Manchester City following Lille’s friendly at Everton, saying: ‘Bouaddi is a very good player. He is available (in terms of his fitness) and he played 45 minutes. But that is only because I have to manage his minutes. Next week we start the season and I consider him as an available player for me.

‘Of course, there are negotiations. There is interest from so many clubs. He is a really, really good player and I hope that he is going to stay with us! What makes him so special? He has a huge personality.

‘He is incredibly intelligent on and off the pitch, he is really mature. He is 18 years old but he looks like he is 32 when he is on the pitch. Technically he is really complete. He is also physical, really strong in duels. He’s going to be one of the best midfielders in Europe for the next 10 years.’

Ayyoub Bouaddi is 'really complete' according to his Lille boss Davide Ancelotti

Chelsea set Neto price tag

Chelsea want close to £100million if they are to sell Pedro Neto this summer, sources inside the Stamford Bridge club have told Daily Mail Sport.

Neto, 26, has had several interested suitors in this window from the Premier League and beyond. Saudi side Al Hilal have been heavily linked this week.

It is understood no formal bids have yet landed with Chelsea for their Portuguese international, but they are aware of others' appreciation.

For more on this story click HERE

KIERAN GILL

Chelsea want in the region of £100million for Pedro Neto

Rodri set for Barca switch

Manchester City midfielder Rodri is expected to arrive in Barcelona this evening.

The Spain captain will then undergo a medical ahead of completing his £64.5million move to the La Liga champions.

Rodri is due to sign a four-year contract on Tuesday and the plan is for him to be unveiled by the club on Wednesday.

Former City full-back Joao Cancelo is also due in Barcelona at lunchtime today after agreeing to return to the club from Al Hilal.

Rodri is set to return to Spain after lifting the World Cup with his country this summer

Vicario lands in Turin after Spurs strike loan deal

Tottenham goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario has arrived in Italy ahead of completing his initial loan move to Juventus.

The deal also includes an £8.5m option to buy the 28-year-old Italy international permanently.

The 29-year-old Italian has been on Juve's list for some time and they reverted to him on Sunday after a move for Aston Villa's Emiliano Martinez collapsed.

Villa are signing Zion Suzuki from Parma in a £30m deal. The Japan international is due to undergo his medical today also.

Guglielmo Vicario is set for Juventus after an £8.5m deal was struck with Spurs

Sunderland set to confirm Methalie deal

Toulouse left-back Dayann Methalie arrived in the UK on Sunday ahead of his medical at Sunderland.

The France U21 international, a former target for Newcastle, is set to finalise his £25.7million move pending today’s tests.

Dedic in for Toon medical

Benfica right-back Amar Dedic arrived on Tyneside last night ahead of undergoing a medical at Newcastle.

Negotiations are at the final stages with a £29.5million deal in place for the 23-year-old.

The Bosnia international is likely to go straight into the team to play Liverpool next weekend.

Newcastle have also held talks with Bayern Munich over a move for Joao Palhinha but have other targets they are considering. Tottenham's Lucas Bergvall is one of the names that remains on their radar in the final days of the window.

Nottingham Forest are also expected to make another offer for the Swede.

Sports.title: Rodri lands in Barcelona ahead of £65.4m move from Man City and declares 'we're going for everything that comes our way'
Sports.content:
Rodri lands in Barcelona ahead of £65.4m move from Man City and declares 'we're going for everything that comes our way'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Rodri has addressed gathered media after landing in Barcelona ahead of finalising his £65.4million move from Manchester City.

The Spain captain said: 'I'm happy to be here; it's been a few intense days, and I'm thrilled to be here.

'Playing for Barcelona is a dream. We're going for the Champions League and everything else that comes our way.'

He will have a medical tomorrow ahead of being officially unveiled potentially on Wednesday.

Rodri will sign a four-year contract until 2030, just a month after he captained Spain to World Cup glory. After a seven-year spell with City, he will now return to his homeland.

He agreed to join Barcelona two weeks ago after informing rivals Real Madrid he no longer wished to join them.

Rodri has arrived in Barcelona ahead of signing for the club from Manchester City

The opening offers, however, fell well below City's demands for £68million.

Discussions have been ongoing with Barca now reaching City's valuation.

He flew to Spain on Monday evening and will now progress with the process of officially becoming a Barcelona player.

Rodri returned to Manchester from his break after winning the World Cup on Thursday, taking a Ryanair flight from Madrid to Liverpool but was not involved in today's Community Shield defeat by Arsenal.

City now intend to press ahead with their move for Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille but still want another midfielder.

Sports.title: Former Sheffield United owner claims Championship side face 12-point deduction in payment row - as club fires back at 'publicity stunt'
Sports.content:
The former owners of Sheffield United have claimed the club could be hit with a 12-point deduction amid a row over payment.

United World, which sold the Championship side to current owners Helmy Eltoukhy and Steven Rosen, is attempting to wind up the company the Americans used to buy the club, claiming they are owed more than £35million.

A hearing is due at the High Court this week and – should it result in further action – United World say the Blades could be docked a potentially season-defining 12 points.

United World is the investment arm of ex-United owner, Saudi Arabian Prince Abdullah Bin Mosaad Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud. It claims that Eltoukhy and Rosen transferred their shares to a new company in June in ‘what appears to be an attempt to avoid paying creditors’ and that, following the transfer, the company which owes them £35m no longer has any assets with which to pay the debt.

The hearing is listed for Wednesday in London.

‘In short, they are trying to take the club without paying for it,’ a United World statement added.

United World, the investment arm of ex-United owner, Saudi Arabian Prince Abdullah have claimed the club could be hit with a 12-point deduction amid a row over payment

Sheffield United's owners have dismissed the statement as being a 'publicity stunt'

‘If the winding-up petition is granted on 19 August, as we expect, EFL Regulation 2.1.16 provides that Rosen must be disqualified from being a controlling owner and director of SUFC. He will no longer be able to be chairman, or a director, he will no longer be able to exercise any control over the club and will have to sell a significant proportion of his controlling interest in the club.

'In addition, we understand that, once investigations are completed, there is a real prospect that the EFL may have to impose a 12-point deduction on SUFC under EFL Regulation 12.3, in order to “protect the integrity and continuity of the League Competition” and “the reputation of The League.”

In an escalating row, sources close to Eltoukhy and Rosen dismissed the statement as a ‘publicity stunt’.

‘We are disappointed Prince Abdullah is trying to hurt the club and its supporters with publicity stunts,’ an insider said.

‘The deal between sophisticated parties in 2024 was well advised by his financial advisors.

‘Sheffield United is financially healthy, unlike under Prince Abdullah when the Club incurred a points deduction for missing payments to football creditors.

‘Nonetheless, Helmy Eltoukhy and Steven Rosen invited Abdullah to re-invest in the club and join the ownership of Sheffield United and to help use his skills to support our promotion efforts.

‘Helmy and Steve are focused on the sustainability of the club and the season ahead.’

Sports.title: Ranking of the best players in world football revealed in EA SPORTS FC27's new ratings - with just ONE Premier League player set to star in the top 10
Sports.content:
Football game company EA Sports have revealed their top-rated players for the upcoming FC27 game, with only one Premier League player making the top ten.

The newest edition of the game, formerly called FIFA, will be fully released on September 25, with fans able to play on PC, PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch and Amazon Luna.

To build anticipation for its release, EA has revealed official ratings, with the gradings for the world's top stars revealed.

There is no outright leader in terms of the highest rated men's players – with Kylian Mbappe and Manchester City striker Erling Haaland both rated 91.

There are then a further nine players just behind them on 90, including Barcelona-bound Rodri – meaning Haaland will be the only Premier League star in the top ten once the Spanish midfielder's transfer to the La Liga champions is confirmed.

Rodri is joined by Ousmane Dembele, Vitinha, Harry Kane, Michael Olise, Pedri, Lamine Yamal, Thibaut Courtois and Jude Bellingham.

There is just one Premier League star among the ten highest-rated men's players in FC27

There are then three Premier League players rated 89 in Gianluigi Donnarumma, Bruno Fernandes and Gabriel.

Mbappe was also the highest-rated men's player in FC26 at 91, joined by Mohamed Salah.

There is, meanwhile, a clear front-runner in the women's selection. Alexia Putellas, who joined London City Lionesses from Barcelona this summer, takes the crown with a 91 rating, closely followed by former team-mate Aitana Bonmati and Khadija Shaw of Manchester City who are rated 90.

More player ratings are set to be released in the coming days, with the top Premier League stars announced at 4pm BST on Tuesday.

Sports.title: Todd Boehly open to selling his stake in Chelsea to majority owners Clearlake Capital four years after taking charge - with Mark Walter also considering sale
Sports.content:
Todd Boehly open to selling his stake in Chelsea to majority owners Clearlake Capital four years after taking charge - with Mark Walter also considering sale

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Todd Boehly and Mark Walter are exploring a sale of their stakes in Chelsea to majority owners Clearlake Capital.

Talks are ongoing over a deal that could value the club at £5billion – although whether an agreement can be struck remains to be seen.

It is understood that discussions have been taking place on and off for the last two years amid differences in strategy between the two American groups who joined forces to buy the club in a forced sale from Roman Abramovich for £2.5bn with a further commitment of a £1.75bn investment in 2022.

While Clearlake owns 61.5 per cent, it shares joint control with Boehly, who is close to the end of a five-year term as chairman. Next May, that role will switch to Clearlake.

Boehly is a co-controlling owner, along with Behdad Eghbali and Jose E Feliciano, who manage the Clearlake investment, with all major decisions having to be signed off by the group.

The remaining 38.5 per cent is split between Boehly, Walter and Swiss business leader Hansjorg Wyss.

Chelsea co-owner Todd Boehly is open to selling his stake in the club, four years after investing

Chelsea insiders have continuously denied claims of a rift between Eghbali and Boehly and are adamant that they maintain a ‘professional and constructive’ relationship.

However, things would appear to be coming to a head.

Earlier this month, Walter sold the NBA’s Los Angeles Lakers just 14 months after buying it. The Wall Street Journal has reported that the US attorney’s office and the Securities and Exchange Commission are investigating the American amid allegations over his business empire.

Sports.title: Sky Sports DROP Baller League after 'partnership came to natural end' - with celebrity-backed competition 'keen to become free-to-air'
Sports.content:
Sky Sports DROP Baller League after 'partnership came to natural end' - with celebrity-backed competition 'keen to become free-to-air'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Sports broadcasting giants Sky Sports have ended their coverage of Baller League from next season after opting not to renew their contract.

The competition, which has since its inception been backed by the likes of KSI, Gary Lineker and Ian Wright, sold out the O2 Arena for last season's final, which was won by KSI's Prime FC.

According to The Guardian, Sky are said to have been happy with viewing figures and social media interaction, but feel the partnership has come to a natural end.

The first UK edition of the tournament, which is an indoor six-a-side competition, took place in 2025 and follows a common trend of the growth in power of influencers.

The teams were usually made up of former professional footballers or those without a club, and have also been managed by the likes of Chloe Kelly and Angry Ginge.

It had first launched in Germany a year prior, inspired by Spain's Kings League, with backing from footballers Mats Hummels and Lukas Podolski.

Sky Sports had ended its partnership with Baller League, who are keen to make the competition free-to-air

Chief executive Felix Starck told The Guardian that the organisation had not tried to extend its deal with Sky and is keen to make its shows free-to-air. It is reported, though, that talks with Comcast, Sky's parent company, did take place.

They are said to now be focusing on expanding their YouTube profile.

The Baller League is made up of 12 teams and there are rolling subs throughout games.

Each team plays each other once in back-to-back matches on Monday nights, with the final four at the end of the season progressing to the semi-finals, before the final decides the winner of the league.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino SACKS FIFA executive after criticism under-fire president
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino SACKS FIFA executive after criticism under-fire president

FIFA's chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, said that he and his colleagues had been 'deceived' by Gianni Infantino's now scrapped plan to sell the World Cup to private investors

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino continues to receive backlash (Image: Jared C. Tilton - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

FIFA has sacked its chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, after he criticised president Gianni Infantino's plan to sell off the World Cup. Lamour, a longtime colleague of Infantino at both FIFA and UEFA, said that staff had been 'deceived' by the plan which has now been scrapped following widespread backlash.

‌



Sky News first reported Lamour's departure. While FIFA chose not to comment on the nature of his exit, football's world governing body did offer a statement.

‌



"FIFA can confirm that the working relationship between FIFA and Kevin Lamour as FIFA's Chief Operating Officer has ended on 17 August 2026," the statement read. "FIFA thanks Kevin for his two years of service and wishes him the best of luck for the future."

‌



A letter sent by FIFA secretary general Mattias Grafstrom has also surfaced. It informed FIFA staff about Lamour's departure, with the Frenchman having been with the organisation since November 2024.

"Following recent discussions, FIFA and our Chief Operating Officer, Kevin Lamour have agreed to part ways," Grafstrom said. "This decision was made after careful consideration and with great respect for Kevin, both personally and professionally.

"Kevin joined FIFA in November 2024 and in this time has overseen a period of significant change, including improved relationships with stakeholders and the delivery of several significant projects of joint interest, amongst many other key achievements.

"You will have seen Kevin present in each FIFA Council meeting since his appointment in 2024, and many of you will have had a regular working relationship with Kevin on projects of various kinds since his joining FIFA.

‌

View 2 Images Kevin Lamour was with FIFA for nearly two years (Image: Joosep Martinson - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

"I felt it was important that I personally provide you this update and I would like to express my gratitude to Kevin for these contributions and for his work and commitment on behalf of FIFA on a daily basis. I wish Kevin all the best for the future." Last month, Lamour made headlines by saying that he and his colleagues were 'deceived' by Infantino's plan to sell FIFA competitions, including the men's World Cup to private investors, labelling it 'the project of one person'. The 45-year-old also suggested that the under-fire president should step down from the position which he's held since 2016.

Article continues below

"Not only must this project not go ahead," Lamour wrote. "But the time has now come for football political leaders to ask themselves the right questions and make the right decisions."

Sports.title: Emma Raducanu could QUIT tennis over injury hell, claims BBC icon
Sports.content:
Emma Raducanu could QUIT tennis over injury hell, claims BBC icon

Emma Raducanu has been forced to miss the upcoming US Open, as the British number one continues to recover from a stress fracture which also ruled her out of Wimbledon

View 2 Images Emma Raducanu's career has been blighted by injuries (Image: Shaun Brooks - CameraSport via Getty Images)

Emma Raducanu has been tipped to announce her shock retirement aged 23. Ex-BBC star Andrew Castle has suggested that Raducanu may've finally 'had enough' of her constant injury setbacks.

‌



The British number one recently pulled out of this year's US Open, which starts next week, due to a stress fracture in her right leg. Raducanu suffered her latest injury during the grass-court season, forcing her to miss Wimbledon .

‌



Castle, who quit his role with the BBC earlier this year, wants to see Raducanu continue but wouldn't be surprised if she decided to call time on her career. The former tennis player told Betway: "Well, put it this way. I mean, I've got no access to that camp whatsoever, but it wouldn't surprise me if one day, out of the blue, she just said, you know, 'I've had enough of all this'.

‌



"I mean, don't we all say that? She doesn't have an obligation to anybody but herself and her family. That's it. There is nothing else. All the sponsors and everybody else, they're not the ones whose career this is.
